Band Mode

One person runs the sync server on a laptop (same WiFi/hotspot as everyone), shares its address, and each phone connects here. Whoever taps "Take control" leads tempo and start/stop for the room — everyone else clicks in sync automatically.

Sound

The metronome speaks the beat numbers instead of clicking, in the counting language set further down. Pick which of your phone’s voices each option should use — these are remembered per language, so Polish and English can have different pairs.

Screen

Hiding the brand header and the tab bar hands their space to the metronome — worth it on a small screen in landscape. Bring them back with a tap just inside the top or bottom edge, or a two-finger tap anywhere.

Screen

Turn off whatever you do not look at on stage. The song title and START are always there, and so are the exit and menu buttons — you would have no way back without them.
Top bar — NOTES, LYRICS and the sync dot. Exit and the menu button stay either way.

Saved screens

Save the switches above under a name, then switch between them from the ≡ menu inside Gig Mode — no need to come back here mid-gig.

Sequencer & section cues

Lyrics view (full-screen lyrics and chords, with a button wherever a song has them)
Lyrics follow the song (jump to the section the metronome is playing)
Section marker sound (extra click on the first beat of a new section)
Show section notes in Gig & Pendulum view (replaces song notes while the section plays). The main screen always shows song and section notes side by side.
Duck the count under section announcements — the numbers keep going, just quieter, so the pulse never drops out
Checking…
Below Female/Male you’ll find every voice installed on this phone, numbered. Current Android voices no longer report whether they’re male or female, so Female/Male only shift the pitch — for a real male voice, go through the numbered ones and pick by ear. More appear once you install extra voice data in Android’s text-to-speech settings.
Count the bar before a section change out loud (one, two, three, four…)
Loops one bar of clicks with the count over it.
Words are aligned so the stressed vowel lands on the beat — the “a” in “raz”, not the “r” — the way a singer counts a band in. Nudge this if your device’s voice still sits early or late.

Volume Levels

What each beat-dot tap cycles through. Add as many as you like — each gets its own color, loudness, and either an auto pitch-shift or a specific click sound.

Foot controller

Control Start/Stop and song navigation from a USB foot pedal — either as keyboard keys (most cheap pedals work this way) or real MIDI (needs the page loaded over HTTPS, from a file, or on this same computer — most local-WiFi setups can't grant MIDI access for security reasons).

Library

Export saves all your songs and setlists to a file you can back up or share. Import loads one back in — you'll be asked whether to replace or merge with what you already have.

CSV is a simpler alternative for songs only (name, bpm, beats/bar, subdivision, pre-count) — handy for editing a song list in Excel/Sheets. Accents, sections, and sound choices aren't included in CSV; use the full JSON export for those.
